RH corresponds to density in L²(0,1); for 1<p<∞, the source equates a zero-free half-plane σ>1/p, density in L^p(0,1), and approximation of the single target χ_(0,1). The p-parameter links the analytic region to the ambient norm, while the characteristic-function condition compresses full density to one distinguished approximation task.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Transforms a zero-location statement into a closure problem, compares full density with single-target membership, and identifies both the representation gain and the absence of an explicit approximating sequence or convergence rate.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted after downgrading the literal coefficient constraint to an extraction report while preserving the zero-free-region, L^p-density, and characteristic-function mechanisms.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span defines N(0,1) through finite sums of fractional-part functions and states the L² and general L^p equivalences. The extraction renders a coefficient constraint as Σc_k=0, but that material formula is withheld as exact training content pending scan verification.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The completeness and p-parameter readings are direct inferences from the stated equivalences. No claim is made that closure is easier to prove, and the extracted constraint is not certified.

parents.title: Dirichlet polynomials approximating the reciprocal of zeta characterize RH

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Rather than invert ζ pointwise, the criterion asks for finite approximants to its reciprocal in a norm that controls aggregate boundary-line error. Increasing polynomial length provides the approximation hierarchy.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: The bridge objects are the Dirichlet mollifier A_N, the residual 1−A_Nζ, and its weighted L² norm on the critical line.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: The span states an RH-equivalent infimum over length-N Dirichlet polynomials whose displayed weighted integral residual tends to zero. It defines A_N as a finite Dirichlet polynomial and states that earlier work had obtained the implication to RH from Nyman-Beurling. The candidate correctly distinguishes norm approximation from pointwise inversion and records the absence of coefficients or a convergence rate. The reciprocal-approximation reading exposes the operation performed by the residual and is not mere restatement.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The source states that RH is equivalent to a weighted integral infimum of |1−A_N(1/2+it)ζ(1/2+it)|² tending to zero as N→∞, where A_N(s)=Σ_{n=1}^N a_n/n^s is any length-N Dirichlet polynomial. It notes that an earlier consequence of Nyman–Beurling supplied one implication.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The criterion gives neither coefficients nor a rate, and small average error need not mean pointwise control. The exact weight and delimiters matter to the equivalence and are damaged in extraction. High for the literal integral: OCR misplaces parentheses, the measure, and the weight. Low for the limiting mollification mechanism and the stated length-N Dirichlet-polynomial class. Interpreting A_N as a finite reciprocal approximant or mollifier follows directly from the residual 1-A_N zeta. Increasing N supplies an approximation hierarchy, while average error alone does not imply pointwise control. The exact measure, weight, parentheses, and delimiters in the integral are damaged; the candidate appropriately avoids reconstructing them and limits confidence to the mollification mechanism.

parents.title: A two-variable Fourier-kernel inequality characterizes real zeros of Xi

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Fourier representation turns real-rootedness into positivity of a kernel expression. The universal quantification over x and y is a certificate family intended to detect any failure of real-zero structure.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: The bridge objects are Xi's Fourier kernel Φ and the associated two-variable integral form; they connect root location to positivity.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: The prose says Polya supplied integral criteria for Fourier transforms to have only real zeros and applies one to the Riemann xi-function. The span states RH if and only if a displayed two-variable integral is nonnegative for all real x and y and then defines Phi by a series. The candidate retains only the secure real-zero-to-integral-positivity mechanism and does not equate the integral condition with pointwise positivity of Phi. The candidate's bridge language is backed by the named Fourier-transform criterion, the kernel Phi, and the quantified integral.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The source states that, after applying one of Pólya's integral criteria to the Riemann ξ-function, RH is equivalent to a displayed double integral involving Φ(α)Φ(β), exponential factors, and (α−β)² being nonnegative for all real x and y. It then gives a series formula for Φ.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The criterion remains an infinite positivity problem and the span gives no reduction to a tractable test set. Positivity here should not be conflated with pointwise positivity of Φ. High for exact training use: exponent placement, imaginary factors, and the formula for Φ are visibly OCR-risky. Only the real-zero-to-integral-positivity mechanism is secure without scan verification. Treating the universally quantified inequalities as a certificate family for real-zero structure is a direct consequence of the stated equivalence. Fourier-kernel representation is the concrete bridge, not a generic representation claim. Exponent placement, imaginary factors, and most of the series for Phi are severely OCR-sensitive; only the qualitative integral-positivity mechanism is reliable without scan verification.

parents.title: Positivity of all Hankel-type determinants characterizes RH

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The coefficient sequence is not tested termwise; overlapping shifts are coupled in structured matrices. Determinant positivity checks joint consistency of all coefficients visible at each finite level.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: The bridge is logarithmic-derivative coefficients → Hankel-type matrices M_n → an infinite sequence of scalar determinant signs.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: The span expands the displayed negative Xi logarithmic derivative into coefficients s_i, defines M_n through entries s_(i+j), and requires det M_n>0 for every n>=1. The candidate correctly distinguishes structured determinant tests from coefficientwise signs. It preserves the universal finite-level hierarchy and does not claim a finite cutoff. 'Moment-like' is cautious analogy; the concrete matrix construction and determinant condition keep it from becoming content-free.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The source expands the displayed negative logarithmic derivative of Xi as s₁+s₂t+s₃t²+…, defines M_n by (M_n)_{ij}=s_{i+j}, and states RH is equivalent to det M_n>0 for every n≥1.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: All finite levels are required, so checking any bounded collection is insufficient. The source does not show that the determinants are easier to control than Xi's zeros or identify a finite obstruction. Moderate for exact notation: Xi-prime is OCR-rendered ambiguously and coefficient indexing should be scan-checked. The matrix/determinant equivalence is otherwise clear. Overlapping coefficient shifts couple the sequence in Hankel-type matrices, so determinant positivity tests joint rather than termwise structure. The coefficients-to-matrices-to-scalar-signs chain is a genuine bridge operation. Xi-prime is rendered like Xi-zero, and the exact coefficient indexing is formula-sensitive, though both the expansion and stated index pattern are visible.

parents.title: A heat-like deformation turns RH into the sign of a real-zero threshold

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The deformation supplies an ordered path through function space, with real-rootedness becoming stable on one side of a critical parameter. RH is recast as whether the original Xi lies inside that stable regime, while Λ=0 would place it exactly at criticality.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: The bridge is the de Bruijn–Newman family Ξ_λ and its threshold Λ, connecting heat-like deformation, real-zero preservation, and the undeformed Xi function.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: The span defines a lambda-parametrized Xi family, states Xi_0=Xi, and gives a threshold Lambda with all zeros real exactly for lambda at or above it. It explicitly states RH if and only if Lambda<=0 and records Newman's conjecture Lambda=0. The candidate correctly treats the numerical lower bound as historical source content and avoids asserting its damaged literal value. 'Heat-like' is interpretive, but the central threshold and deformation operations are explicit and carry the analysis.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The source defines a family Ξ_λ from Φ by an integral transform with a λ-dependent Gaussian factor and states Ξ_0=Ξ. It states that there is Λ with Ξ_λ having only real zeros exactly when λ≥Λ, and that RH is equivalent to Λ≤0. It also records Newman's conjecture Λ=0 and a historical numerical lower bound.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: Existence of the threshold does not determine its sign, and the historical lower bound in this 2004 source is not current evidence. The unit does not derive monotonicity or the threshold theorem. High for the exact deformation and numerical constant: signs, exponents, an oscillatory factor, and scientific notation are OCR-ambiguous. Low for the threshold statement and RH⇔Λ≤0 as source claims. The threshold organizes the family into an ordered real-rooted and non-real-rooted regime. If Lambda=0, the undeformed member lies at the threshold, so the criticality reading follows from Xi_0=Xi and the threshold statement. The sign of the lambda term, exponents, oscillatory factor, Phi formula, and historical scientific notation are damaged; the candidate prudently leaves these exact details unresolved.

parents.title: A divisibility matrix encodes RH in determinant growth

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The Redheffer construction encodes divisibility incidence in an explicit finite 0–1 matrix and makes determinant growth the aggregate matrix observable whose asymptotic exponent is stated to be RH-equivalent. The separately listed spectral radius, multiplicities, and nontrivial-eigenvalue estimates are auxiliary observables; the span does not show that they imply the determinant criterion. A computation at any fixed n therefore cannot settle the universally asymptotic condition.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Maps divisibility to finite-dimensional linear algebra and distinguishes determinant growth from individual spectral diagnostics, stating precisely what the encoding aggregates without inventing an arithmetic-cancellation mechanism.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted after removing the unsupported cancellation explanation and retaining the fixed-n limitation, the determinant/spectrum boundary, and the OCR risk.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span gives the exact entry rule for A(n), states det A(n)=O(n^(1/2+ε)) for every ε>0 as equivalent to RH, and separately reports unconditional, RH-conditional, and conjectural spectral information. Several radicals and comparison symbols in those ancillary estimates are corrupted, while the matrix rule and determinant exponent remain prose-recoverable.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The divisibility-to-matrix bridge and determinant-versus-spectrum distinction are grounded in the span. The unit-disc remark remains source-attributed possibility, not accepted fact.
